newsitem.title: USA: NYMEX electricity lower with natgas, spot power.
newsitem.headline: NYMEX electricity lower with natgas, spot power.

text.p: NYMEX electricity futures were trading lower Friday in line with weaker natural gas futures and U.S. West spot power prices, industry sources said.
"Basically electricity is following the natural gas market," said one Houston-based futures trader.

As of 1230 EDT, June Palo Verde (PV) futures were trading down 83 cents at $21.90 following exchanges in a range of $21.50-22.20, while July PV was down 48 cents at $25.20 following exchange in a range of $25.00-25.40 per MWh.

June California Oregon Border (COB) was trading down 34 cents at $16.10 following trades in a range of $15.75-16.25, while July was down 20 cents at $17.50 following exchanges in a range of $17.30-17.60 per MWh.
NYMEX said that as of 1150 EDT and estimated total of 176 PV and 210 COB contracts had traded.
Natural gas futures were also trading lower, with June NYMEX Henry Hub futures down 3.8 cents at $2.235 per million British thermal units as of 1225 EDT.
Western physical power prices were also quoted lower, with peak firm Saturday to Monday PV talked at $26.00-27.00 pe MWh.
Although over 8,000 megawatts (MW) of power generation in the U.S. West remained off line for refueling or maintenance, much of that capacity was expected to return to service through the month.
"Overall we're looking at about 1,500 MW of power returning to service in the West (over the next week)," said the Houston-based trader.

Weather in the Pacific Northwest was expected to turn cooler Saturday with a rain threat, while Sunday and Monday were expected to be sunny and warm, averaging three to six degrees above normal through the period.

In the Southwest, southern California and southwest Arizona were expected to be sunny and hot with maximum temperatures of over 100 degrees Fahrenheit. Other areas were called to see scattered thunderstorms in the afternoons, especially in the mountain areas.
